ingredients.name: Jaggery or brown sugar or maple syrup

recipes.name: Aloo Gobhi
steps: Blend the green chilies and ginger to make a paste.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for a few seconds. Then add the chili paste and saute for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the turmeric, red chili powder, ground coriander, ground cumin and salt, and stir to combine.

When the tomatoes have cooked down and the oil separates, add the potatoes and stir. Cover and cook for a few minutes until the potatoes are about half done. Add a bit of water, if necessary, to prevent them from burning.
Add in the cauliflower. Cover and cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Once the cauliflower and potato are cooked, add garam masala and give a final mix.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobhi (Spiced Cauliflower & Potato)

ingredients.prep_notes: medium, cut into wedges; range listed as 2-3

steps: Blend green chilies and ginger into a paste.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then add chili paste and saute 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook 2-3 minutes.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, ground coriander, ground cumin, and salt.
When tomatoes cook down and oil separates, add potatoes and cover; cook until half done.
Add a little water if needed to prevent sticking.
Add cauliflower, cover, and cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally.
When potato and cauliflower are done, stir in garam masala.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi Mutter Sabzi
steps: For Masala Mixture: In a bowl add water, turmeric powder, red chill powder, hing, jeera powder and mix everything properly then keep aside for further use
Cut the cauliflower into florets and keep aside. Wash them just before use and not in advance.
Take a pot add some oil and saute the cauliflower in that (on high flame) until 50% cooked
Do not add salt while sauteeing the cauliflower. Once half cooked leave it aside to add to the curry later
In a pot heat oil. Add cumin seeds, ginger, green chillies, garlic and saute for a few seconds then add the prepared masala mixture
Saute until the oil starts separating. Add tomato and saute until cooked. Then add peas and potatoes, salt and mix everything properly.
Then cover and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes until potatoes are half cooked. Add a bit of water to ensure that the vegetables dont burn.
Once potatoes are 50% done add the cauliflower and mix. Cover and cook until the vegetables are cooked. Garnish with chopped cilantro

recipes.name: Aloo Tamatar Sabzi

ingredients.prep_notes: medium, peeled and diced into 1-inch cubes

steps: In a pot, heat mustard oil over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and fennel seeds, and let splutter well.
Add the asafoetida, crushed green chilies and ginger. Saute for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric, red chili powder and ground coriander, and saute for another minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook until fragrant. Then add the potatoes and mix well.
Pour in enough water to cover the mixture and add the salt. Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the potatoes are done.
Increase the heat to high, remove the lid and mash some of the potatoes with a masher, and continue to cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the ghee, place into a serving bowl, and garnish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Aloo, Matar, Tamatar Sabzi
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and saute asafoetida and cumin seeds until seeds darken.
Add crushed green chilies and potatoes; stir to coat with oil.
Add salt and a sprinkling of water, cover, and steam potatoes.
When potatoes are halfway done, add ground coriander and red chili powder; add more water if needed.
Saute 2 minutes, then add cilantro, frozen peas, and tomato.
Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are done but not mushy.
Stir in roasted ground cumin and serve.

recipes.name: Amti (Marathi Dal)
steps: Wash and soak the toor dal for 1 hour. Pressure cook it until soft with about 4x water. Keep aside.
Thaw coconut to room temperature. Soak tamarind in warm water for 1 hour and prepare tamarind pulp. Keep aside
Heat oil in pan, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds. Reduce the heat to low and add hing, turmeric, red chilly powder, and goda masala.
Take care that the spices do not burn. Add curry leaves, chilly paste, handful of chopped cilantro. Saute for 1 minute.
Add water to this mixture and bring it to a rapid boil. Add salt to taste. Once boiling, add the cooked toor dal to it and mix it well until the dal is properly mixed in
Add tamarind pulp, jaggery and coconut and simmer for 3-4 minutes on low flame.
Garnish with cilantro and serve!

recipes.name: Avial

ingredients.prep_notes: unripe, outer skin peeled, cut into slices
or half packet if using frozen
whisked; substitute 1 tbsp lemon juice for vegan
or to taste, for coconut paste

steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature.
Make the coconut paste by grinding the coconut, green chilies and water.
Prepare the plantain and keep it in a bowl of water to prevent discoloration. Cut all the vegetables into approximately 2-inch pieces. If using frozen yam, use as is.

In a medium-sized saucepan, bring the water and salt to a boil. Add the turmeric and drumsticks, and cook for 3 minutes. Next, add the plantains and simmer for 2 minutes until both vegetables are partially cooked. Then, add the long beans, winter melon, and yam, cooking the mixture until all are fork-tender but not falling apart.
Once all the vegetables are cooked, add the coconut paste and continue to simmer over low heat for 1-2 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the yogurt, coconut oil and curry leaves, and serve.

recipes.name: Beetroot Thoran
steps: Peel the beetroot and cut off the base and top. Cut it in 4 quarters. Now grate all through a food processor thick blade.
Keep aside. Slice onions and keep aside. Make a coarse paste of coconut, green chillies and jeera
Take coconut oil in a pot. Once hot add mustard seeds, once they splutter add curry leaves and turmeric powder
Add the grated beetroot and salt and give it a good mix. Cover and let it cook on low flame for 2-3 minutes
Uncover and mix. Add some water to help the beetroot cook well. Cover and cook the beetroot well. If it needs more water add some along the way
Once the beetroot is cooked you dont want any leftover water, so be careful to not add too much water
Add the ground coconut paste and give it a good mix. Turn off the flame and cover and let it sit for 5 minutes

recipes.name: Bhindi Aloo Pyaaz
steps: Wash the whole okra and let it dry for 3-4 hours, or overnight.
When ready to cook, heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, dried red chilies, garlic, onion and potato, and cook until the potato is about halfway done, about 7-8 minutes.
Add the turmeric and red chili powder, followed by the okra, and stir.
If the heat is too low, the okra can become slimy; if too high, the vegetables can burn, so aim for medium heat.
After about 3-4 minutes, add the ground coriander, dried raw mango powder, garam masala and salt, and mix well to combine. Continue to saute until the vegetables are cooked.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Black & Pinto Beans
steps: Soak black and pinto beans overnight and add a bit of salt and baking soda to the soaking solution. Drain in the morning and wash once
Pressure cook the beans with bay leaves, 1/3 of the onion, some garlic. Once the pressure cook has its first whistle lower the flame to minimum and cook the beans for 45 minutes
Let the pressure drop normally. Open the cooker and discard the bay leaves and take out extra liquid and store on the side
Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat with half the oil. Once hot, add the onion and garlic with a pinch of salt and cook until the onion has softened and is golden
Add the garlic, jalapeño, cumin powder, mexican oregano, black pepper, and paprika. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the black beans with some of liquid and bring to a simmer until thickened and saucy. If it gets too thick, add the reserve water from the pressure cooker
Add lemon juice, Garnish with cilantro, and adjust for salt
Final texture of the beans should be saucy, not dry, separate beans

recipes.name: Black Beans
steps: Soak black beans overnight and add a bit of salt and baking soda to the soaking solution. Drain in the morning and wash once
Pressure cook the beans with bay leaves, 1/3 of the onion, some garlic. Once the pressure cook has its first whistle lower the
flame to minimum and cook the beans for 45 minutes
Let the pressure drop normally. Open the cooker and discard the bay leaves and take out extra liquid and store on the side
Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat with half the oil. Once hot, add the onion and garlic with a pinch of salt and cook until the onion
has softened and is golden
Add the garlic, jalapeño, cumin powder, mexican oregano, black pepper, and paprika. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the black beans with some of liquid and bring to a simmer until thickened and saucy. If it gets too thick,
add the reserve water from the pressure cooker
Add lemon juice, Garnish with cilantro, and adjust for salt
Final texture of the beans should be saucy, not dry, separate beans

recipes.name: Black Chana Curry (Gujarati Style)
steps: Wash the black chana, then cover by at least 2 inches of water and soak for 8-9 hours, or overnight.
When ready to cook, rinse the chana, place in a pot with fresh water and add salt. Cook until the chana is soft, about 1 hour.

In a separate pot, heat the oil over medium-low heat and add the carom seeds. Then add the asafoetida and curry leaves and saute for 5-7 seconds. Once they splutter, add the gram flour and saute until it turns light brown in color.
Mash half a cup of the boiled black chana with water to make a paste, and add it to the seasoning. Then add in the rest of the chana, and mix well.
Add the red chili powder, turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, jaggery and tamarind water. Mix well and saute for another minute.
Add 1 1/2 cups water, mix well and cook for 8-10 minutes until the curry thickens, stirring occasionally. Adjust the consistency to your taste.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Black Chana Curry (North Indian)
steps: Wash the black chana, then cover by at least 2 inches of water and soak overnight.

When ready to cook, discard the soaking water and place the chana in a pot with 3 cups fresh water and some salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-high heat until the chana is soft, about 40 minutes. If not soft, continue simmering and add more water as needed.
In a separate pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and asafoetida, and saute until the cumin seeds darken.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, and green chilies, and saute for 3-4 minutes, until the onion turn golden brown. Add the tomatoes and cook until the oil starts to separate.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander, ground cumin, garam masala and red chili powder and cook well.
Add the boiled black chana along with its cooking water, as well as the salt.
Let the mixture simmer for about 10 minutes. Add water to desired consistency (the gravy should be thin for this recipe but you can adjust it according to your preference).
Crush the kasuri methi leaves and add to the chana.
Garnish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Cabbage Poriyal
steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature.
Blend the coconut, red chilies and cumin seeds into a coarse paste (do not add water).
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, urad dal and chana dal, and fry until the dals are golden brown.
Add the curry leaves and asafoetida, and saute for a few seconds before adding the shredded cabbage, turmeric and salt. Saute for 1-2 minutes.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally.
Add the coconut paste to the cabbage, and mix to combine. Saute uncovered for about 2 minutes. The cabbage should keep its crunch, so be careful not to overcook.
Mix in the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.name: Cabbage Sambharo
steps: Salt chopped cabbage and let it rest for 1 hour to release moisture.
Squeeze out water and set cabbage aside.
Heat oil and saute mustard seeds, asafoetida, green chili, and curry leaves for 1 minute.
Add tomato, carrots, and bell pepper and saute about 1 minute.
Add turmeric, coriander, garam masala, lemon/lime juice, and sugar.
Pour cooked mixture over shredded cabbage and toss well.
Garnish with cilantro and green grapes.

recipes.name: Cabbage Sambhraro (Salad)
steps: Shred the cabbage into thin, long pieces,Add salt and let it sit to remove excess water. Squeeze out the water and set aside.
Finely chop the cilantro
Thinly slice the carrot and bell pepper.
Cube the tomatoes.
Cut green chilies into 1-inch pieces.
Heat up oil in a pan. Once hot add mustard seeds, hing, green chillies and curry leaves , then add tomatoes carrot and bell Pepper.
Cook until half done, Then add all the spices ( turmeric, coriander power, garam masala, Lemon juice and sugar)
Turn off the heat and mix the cooked mixture with the shredded cabbage.
Adjust salt and lemon juice based on taste
Garnish with chopped cilantro and Green grapes

recipes.name: Carrot Moong Dal Salad

ingredients.prep_notes: peeled and grated; range listed as 4-5

steps: Thaw coconut to room temperature.
Soak moong dal for 1 hour, drain, and transfer to a mixing bowl.
Add grated carrots.
Crush chopped green chili with salt and add to the carrot-moong mixture.
Prepare tempering by heating oil and adding mustard seeds; once sputtering add urad dal and asafoetida.
When urad dal turns golden, add curry leaves until spluttering.
Pour tempering over carrot mixture.
Add coconut, lemon/lime juice, and cilantro; toss and serve.

recipes.name: Cauliflower Pickle
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the cauliflower and blanch for 1 minute. Remove and pat dry with a kitchen towel.
Toast the spice mix seeds in a pan, then grind into a fine powder.
Place the cauliflower in a bowl along with the red chili powder, salt, turmeric and the ground spices. Mix well and keep aside.
To make the tadka, heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal, chana dal, red chilies and garlic, and fry until it turns golden brown.
Add the curry leaves and asafoetida hing, then remove from the heat.
When the tadka is cool, add it to the cauliflower, and mix well. Stir in the lime juice.
Mix well and allow it to sit covered for 12-24 hours, and enjoy.
Store in a glass container in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Chai
steps: Take one big vessel for the above mentioned quantities. If not, divide it into two small pots.
Boil water with ginger, chai masala and mint leaves. Let it boil for good 10 minutes. Then add chai patti and let it boil for 5 minutes.
Add Milk and just before it comes to boil add lemongrass, cardamom powder. Let it all boil together for 10 minutes and it’s ready to serve.
Ambe mor rice
Mung Dal (Green, Split)
Water
Turmeric powder
Black pepper
Salt
Wash the rice and dal and set aside for about an hour. In a large pot combine the rice, dal and water. Bring it to a boil
Add turmeric and black peppercorns and let it cook on medium flame. Add salt once the khichdi is almost done and mix well
Keep stirring and add water if needed. The final consistency should be a thick porridge like; not dry like Pulav

recipes.name: Chai for Sir

ingredients.prep_notes: such as Brooke Bond Red Label tea powder

steps: Add the water and milk to a saucepan and bring to a simmer on medium high heat, about 2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the tea powder. Boil for 2-3 minutes until the tea becomes a nice brown color.
Add the sugar and continue to cook for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and let the tea sit for 1 minute for the flavors to infuse.
Strain and serve.

recipes.name: Chai Strong, Lightly Spiced
steps: Using a mortar and pestle, crush the ginger together with the cardamom pods.
Warm the water in a small pot until hot, but not boiling.
Add the milk, stir, and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the tea along with the crushed ginger and cardamom. Boil for 4-6 minutes.
Strain and serve.
Add sugar to taste if desired.

recipes.name: Chole Masala
steps: Important prep: Wash, rinse and soak chole (chickpeas), and the chana dal for at least 8 hours
Boil chole with salt, hing, and ginger powder
Heat oil in pan, add bay leaf and cumin seeds. Add ginger paste
Add chopped tomato (alternatively blend tomatoes in Vitamix and add)
Cook till the tomato dries up
Add chana masala and coriander powder, turmeric powder to tomato and saute well for a few mins
Add masala to chole and cook on high flame for about 10 minutes till it thickens slightly. Keep stirring while it cooks
Add half the chopped cilantro while it is still cooking
Mash some chana to give it thicker consistency and also add boiled water if necessary (consistency of final dish should be semi thick)
Add garam masala, kasuri methi, and first taste. Then add lemon juice based on the taste.
Garnish with the remaining chopped cilantro

recipes.name: Chow Chow Raita
steps: Wash, peel, deseed, and grate chayote squash.
Heat oil, add urad dal, mustard, cumin, asafoetida, curry leaves, and green chilies; splutter 5-10 seconds.
Add grated chayote and salt and saute for 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and cool completely.
Whisk yogurt and fold into cooled squash mixture.
Adjust salt and garnish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Cilantro Crema
steps: Pour water into the blender. Add all the ingredients and blend until smooth and creamy
Taste for seasoning, and add more as needed. The crema should be tangy, creamy, and have a slight kick to it!

recipes.name: Coconut Chutney

ingredients.prep_notes: tempering, finely chopped; range listed as 5-6

steps: Thaw frozen coconut to room temperature.
Blend coconut, green chilies, daliya, ginger, salt, lemon juice, and water to a thick smooth paste.
Add cilantro near the end and pulse briefly.
Heat oil in a small pan and saute urad dal until golden.
Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add cumin seeds, dried red chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida; sizzle for about 10 seconds.
Pour tempering into ground paste, mix well, and adjust salt.
Serve with upma.

recipes.name: Coconut Rice with Vegetables
steps: Wash the rice and soak in water for about 30 minutes, then drain.
In a pot, heat the oil over medium heat and add the black pepper, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, fennel seeds and cinnamon, and saute the spices until they become aromatic.

Add the green chilies, crushed ginger and garlic, and saute well. Add the onions and saute until they soften slightly. Add the peas and carrot, followed by the mint and salt, and saute until the mint shrinks slightly.
Combine the water and coconut milk, pour into the vegetables, and stir.

Bring everything to a rolling boil and add the drained rice, stirring gently. Cook uncovered over medium heat until the water from the surface has been absorbed. Cover, lower the heat, and cook for another 15 minutes.
Switch off the heat and let the rice sit covered for 5 more minutes.
Fluff gently, and garnish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Cucumber Carrot Salad
steps: Combine cucumber, carrots, cilantro, ginger, and green chilies in a bowl.
Add lime/lemon juice, black pepper, roasted ground cumin, and salt.
Mix thoroughly and serve.

recipes.name: Cucumber Pachadi
steps: Thaw coconut to room temperature.
Grind coconut, green chilies, mustard seeds, and about 1/4 cup yogurt into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil, add diced cucumber, salt, and a splash of water; cook until soft.
Add coconut paste and cook on low 1-2 minutes until raw smell disappears; mixture should be thick and slightly coarse.
Cool mixture, then fold in remaining yogurt.
Prepare tempering by heating oil with curry leaves, mustard seeds, and dried red chilies.
Pour tempering over pachadi and serve.

recipes.name: Cucumber Raita

ingredients.prep_notes: regular or Greek; or plant-based yogurt for vegan

steps: Whisk yogurt until smooth.
Add roasted ground cumin, salt, and cucumber; mix well.
Garnish with cilantro.
Mix close to serving time so cucumber does not release too much water.

recipes.name: Cucumber Tomato Koshimbir
steps: Combine cucumber, tomatoes, and onion in a bowl.
Add peanuts, lemon/lime juice, green chili, and salt; mix.
Heat oil and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, asafoetida, and curry leaves for 5-10 seconds.
Pour tempering into salad and toss well.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Cucumber Tomato Onion Raita
steps: Mix cucumber, tomatoes, onion, and cilantro into whisked yogurt.
Add salt and roasted ground cumin.
Chill 30-60 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Cucumber, Carrot, Tomato Salad
steps: Need gloves when making salad. Make sure gloves dont get cut when chopping by knife or food processor
Make the dressing by mixing all the items above
Thinly slice carrots and cucumbers in the food processor. Make 1 inch pieces of tomato (dont cut it too fine, 8-10 pieces of each tomato is good)
Mix the dressing with the vegetables and serve

recipes.name: Dal Makhni

ingredients.prep_notes: 1-inch piece, peeled and minced, for chili paste

steps: Wash the urad dal, kidney beans and chana dal, then cover by at least 2 inches of water and soak overnight.
When ready to cook, make a paste of garlic, ginger and green chilies.
Place the dals and beans in a pot with 4 1/2 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until soft, about 1 hour.
Mash the beans slightly with the back of a ladle and add hot water as needed to adjust the consistency (it should be thick, but pourable, like pancake batter).
In a heavy saucepan, heat the ghee or oil over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and saute until they begin to darken. Add the chili paste, tomato paste and asafoetida, and stir for 1 minute.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the red chili powder, turmeric, salt and the cooked beans. Mix well. Increase the heat and bring to a boil, then lower and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
To finish, add the heavy cream (or coconut milk), garam masala, kasuri methi, and cilantro.

recipes.name: Dal Nagori
steps: Important prep: Wash and soak the dals for 4 hours, preferably overnight
Boil : Add soaked dal, water, turmeric, salt to taste and cook in a large pot until cooked
Alternatively you can pressure cook the dal - once cooker is at pressure let it cook for 20 minutes on low flame
Prep the vegetables: grate onion in food processor, puree the tomatoes, make ginger-garlic-chilly paste. Finely chop cilantro. Soak kasuri methi in water
In a pot add oil. Once hot, add dry red chillies, asafoetida, ginger+garlic+chilly paste, onion and saute it well until translucent.
Add half the chopped cilantro, and saute for a minute.
Add turmeric powder, red chilly powder, tomatoes, soaked dry fenugreek leaves and cook for a while on medium flame until the tomatoes are fully cooked
Add water, cooked dal and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes on low flame.
Add salt to taste and let it simmer
Take a portion out for vegans (optional to add another tadka with oil+red chilly powder on top)
Ghee tempering: for the main dal, heat up ghee in a small pan. Once the ghee is medium-hot, switch off the flame, and add red chilly powder to it.
Take care that the tempering does not burn. It should retain a deep red color. Add the seasoning to the dal and garnish with the remaining cilantro

recipes.name: Dal Tadka
steps: Wash the dal and soak in water for 1-2 hours.

Strain the dal, then place it in a pot with 4 cups fresh water, and stir in the turmeric and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the dal is tender (approximately about 20-30 minutes).

Heat the ghee (or oil) over medium heat in a medium-sized pot. Add the cumin seeds, asafoetida and red chilies, and saute for 1 minute. Pour in the cooked dal and mix well to combine. Add hot water if needed to adjust the consistency (it should be medium thick).
Add lemon juice and chopped cilantro, and serve.

recipes.name: Drumstick and plantain Sambar
steps: Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times in water and soak it with 3x water and some hing and a few drops of oil for 2-4 hours
Pressure cook it: once the pot is at full pressure reduce the heat and let it cookfor 15 minutes
Switch off the flame and let the pressure drop naturally
Once the pressure drops, open the lid and whisk the cooked dal together until its smooth
Soak the tamarind in hot water for an hour. Squeeze it with your hands and remove the pulp and set aside
Dice the onions, tomatoes into 1 inch cubes. Slightly peel and chop drumsticks into 2 inch pieces.
Prep the plantains by removing the thin green layer with a peeler (not the full skin), chop it in 1 inch cubes and store in water
In a large pot add all the vegetables and some water and bring it to a boil and let it cook until the vegetables are about half cooked
Add the tamarind paste and half the sambar powder and let the vegetables cook completely
Add the boiled dal, salt, turmeric and mix and let it simmer. Add the remaining sambar powder as needed. Add salt
Prepare tempering: Heat oil and add mustard. When it splutters, add methi, jeera, hing. Then add red chillies and curry leaves
Add the tempering to the sambar, let it simmer, and garnish with chopped cillantro

recipes.name: Filter Coffee

ingredients.prep_notes: brands such as Narasu, Cothas, Kumbakonam, Idhayam; typically 80% coffee 20% chicory powder

steps: For this recipe, you will need a South Indian coffee filter, available at Indian grocery stores or online.
Bring a half cup water to a rolling boil.
Place the coffee into the top part of the filter, attach it to the bottom part, and pat it down lightly (some filters have a small insert for this).
Add half the hot water to the coffee, cover, and let it sit for 30-45 seconds. Then add the remaining water and cover.
Let it sit for at least 20 minutes until all the water has dripped through. You will now have a thick coffee decoction collected in the lower container.
In a small pot, bring 1 cup milk plus 1 cup water to a boil. Add the sugar, if desired.
Switch off the heat and add the coffee decoction to it. For stronger coffee, add more decoction and for lighter add less.
Strain the coffee into a container with a lip. To serve, pour it into a cup from a height so it creates a layer of froth on the top.

recipes.name: Ginger Chai

ingredients.prep_notes: peeled and grated, organic is most flavorful

steps: Place the water and the grated ginger in a pot over medium-high heat and let it come to a rolling boil.
Cover the pot and reduce the heat slightly to intensify the ginger flavor. Simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Add the milk and stir as it boils, being careful not to let it overflow.
Immediately turn off the heat, then add the tea leaves and sugar (if desired). Cover the pan and let the tea steep for 4 minutes.
Strain into serving cups and serve hot.

recipes.name: Green cabbage koshimbir
steps: Remove the frozen grated coconut from the freezer and let it thaw completely
Thinly slice the cabbage in the food processor. Finely chop onion in food processor (pulse lightly). Make green chilly paste
Finely chop cilantro and curry leaves and set aside (separately)
Mix cabbage, onion, green chiillies, coconut, and add salt to taste
To make the seasoning heat coconut oil, add mustard seeds, hing, curry leaves and a handful of chopped cilantro
Add the seasoning to the cabbage mix. Add cilantro and mix everything well and serve

recipes.name: Green Cabbage Salad
steps: Thaw coconut to room temperature.
Mix cabbage, onion, coconut, cilantro, lemon/lime juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat coconut oil for tempering and add mustard seeds.
When mustard pops, add asafoetida and curry leaves; let curry leaves splutter.
Pour hot tempering over salad and toss well.
Garnish with more cilantro.

recipes.name: Green Moong Dal Khichdi
recipes.notes: Maharashtra. V / GF. Spiced with Vegetables.

ingredients.prep_notes: chopped into 1-inch cubes, such as peas, cauliflower, carrots, butternut squash, sweet potato, fava beans
or oil (peanut and coconut work well), for seasoning

steps: Wash the rice and moong dal together in cold water 4-5 times.
Add to a pot with 6 cups of water and soak for 30-60 minutes.
Meanwhile, grind the dried coconut slices, cilantro, curry leaves, green chilies and ginger to make a paste.
After soaking, bring the rice and dal with the turmeric to a boil in the same soaking water.
Lower the heat and simmer until all the water is absorbed and the rice and dal are fully cooked. Add the salt and mix with a wooden spoon for a minute until creamy and porridge-like in consistency.

Make the seasoning by heating the ghee or oil in a pan over medium heat and adding the bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cumin seeds and asafoetida. Add the chopped vegetables and saute on medium heat until al dente. Add the coconut paste and saute for 2-3 minutes and coconut paste, and sauteing for a few minutes.
Add the seasoning to the khichdi and mix well before serving.

recipes.name: Green Papaya Salad

ingredients.prep_notes: cut into 1-inch pieces; range listed as 8-10
1 head, chopped into long thin strips

steps: Prepare and combine all salad ingredients except peanuts in a bowl.
Whisk dressing ingredients (soy sauce, garlic, green chili, lime juice, sugar, salt) until emulsified.
Pour dressing over salad and toss well.
Refrigerate 30 minutes for flavors to develop.
Garnish with peanuts before serving.

recipes.name: Green Plantain Poriyal
steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature.

Trim the ends of the plantains and peel off a thin layer of the skin. Cut vertically and slice into half-inch thick pieces. Soak the pieces in water with a pinch of salt while you assemble and prepare the other ingredients.
Prepare the coconut paste by coarsely grinding together the coconut, cumin seeds, green chilies, curry leaves and salt.

To a large pot add the soaked plantains and enough of their soaking water to fully cover them. Cook on a low heat until they are soft, but not fully cooked, about 8-10 minutes. Check periodically to make sure the water has not evaporated, which can cause the plantains to stick to the pan and burn.

While the plantains are cooking, heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat. Add the chana dal, urad dal and mustard seeds. When the mustard seeds begin to pop, add the dried red chilies, asafoetida and curry leaves. Saute for 10-15 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until it is translucent.
Once the plantains are done and the water has mostly evaporated, add the onion mix and stir thoroughly to combine. Then add the ground coconut paste, and mix well.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt to taste. Saute for 3-4 minutes until all flavors are incorporated.

recipes.name: Green Salad with Tahini Vinaigrette Dressing
steps: To make the dressing:
Roast sesame seeds until golden brown. Blend all the ingredients until you have a smooth paste. The dressing thickens a bit after resting
At the time of mixing the dressing in the salad, if the dressing is too thick add some water to it
Prep all the veggies:
Need gloves when making salad. Make sure gloves dont get cut when chopping by knife or food processor
Slice the cucumber, purple cabbage. Shred the carrots (thick grater). Cube the tomatoes into 1 inch cubes
Wash and cut the romaine lettuce into bite sized pieces
Toss the salad
Mix all the veggies. Add the dressing just before serving and mix thoroughly

recipes.name: Green Salad with Vegan Ranch Dressing
steps: Need gloves when making salad. Make sure gloves dont get cut when chopping by knife or food processor
Dressing: simply blend the ingredients in vitamix until smooth. Add water as needed
The dressing should be of a creamy consistency and it thickens slightly with time
Wash and drain the lettuce and let it dry. Cut the lettuce into bite sized pieces. Thinly slice the cabbage and onions.
Cut the tomatoes, cucumbers and bell peppers into 1 inch cubes
In a large bowl, add everything except dressing.
Just before serving drizzle the dressing over the salad bowl. Use 2 wooden spoons and toss until everything is evenly coated.

recipes.name: Guacamole
steps: Slice the avocados in half, remove the pit, and scoop into a mixing bowl. Husk and chop the tomatillos.
Mash the avocado with a potato masher and make it as chunky or smooth as you'd like
Finely chop the onions and cut the tomatoes into small cubes
Add all ingredients EXCEPT the tomatoes and mix. Give it a taste test and add a pinch more salt or lime juice if needed.
Add the chopped tomatoes at the very end so they dont change the color of the guacamole
For storing keep the pits in the guacamole and remove when ready to serve. Also cover with cling wrap pressing it to the surface
Serve separately on the side:
Romaine Lettuce
Baby spinach
Wash the lettuce and pat dry. Cut into bite sized pieces and serve the lettuce and baby spinach mixed with the meal.

recipes.name: Gujarati Dal
steps: Wash Toor dal and soak for 1-2 hours. Chop tomatoes into 1 inch cubes
Pressure Cook dal with turmeric and a little salt (1:3 water ratio) and then whisk it into a paste and keep it aside.
Heat oil – add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, cloves, cinnamon, methi seeds, dried red chillies, hing
Add curry leaves, ginger paste, green chilli paste and saute well
Then add tomatoes, turmeric powder, coriander cumin powder, red chilli powder and cook till the tomatoes turn mushy
Add jaggery and tamarind paste. Add cooked dal to this tempering
Add 4 cups of water and adjust the dal consistency as required. Add garam masala and aachar masala.
Boil it for sometime and garnish it with chopped cilantro

recipes.name: Gujarati Kadhi
steps: In a bowl whisk together the gram flour (besan), green chilly-ginger paste, yogurt, and salt with water
Beat to a smooth mixture without any lumps.
In a saucepan heat ghee, add methi seeds, cumin seeds, cinnamon, cloves, hing, red chillies and curry leaves
Add the yogurt-water mixture which we had prepared earlier. Stir and mix well.
Bring it to a boil on medium-low to medium heat stirring occassionally so the mixture doesnt separate
Continue to simmer until the raw taste of besan is gone and the kadhi thickens. Add sugar and mix till it dissolves
Garnish with chopped cilantro before serving

recipes.name: Halwai Aloo Sabzi
steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into 1 inch cubes. Dice the tomatoes. Finely chop the cilantro. Coarsely crush the ginger and green chillies
In a pot, heat mustard oil, add cumin seeds, fennel seeds let it splutter well.
Add the asafoetida, crushed chillies & ginger saute for a minute.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder saute for a minute.
Add tomato and saute until fragrant. Then add the potatoes and mix it well.
Add water, salt to taste, and stir it once then put the lid on and cover and let it cook on low-medium flame until the potatoes are fully cooked
Remove the lid and with the help of a masher mash some of the potatoes and then boil it for a minute.
Take a portion aside for vegan serving and garnish with cilantro.
For the rest, finish the dish by adding a little ghee and garnish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Instant Tomato Pickle
steps: Heat half the oil over medium-low heat in a heavy bottomed pan and add the chopped tomatoes and turmeric. Mix well. Cover and cook until the tomatoes are soft and much of their liquid has evaporated.
Add the tamarind paste to allow it to soften.
Remove from the heat and cool to room temperature. Once cool, blend into a smooth paste.
In a pan, roast 1 tablespoon mustard seeds and fenugreek until golden brown and aromatic. Allow them to cool and grind them into a powder.
In the same pan, heat the remaining half of the oil and add 1 teaspoon mustard seeds. Once they start popping, add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds or until slightly softened.
Add the red chili powder and asafoetida to the hot oil and give it a quick stir.
Stir in the ground tomato paste and mix well. Add the salt and mix well until oil begins to ooze out, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the fenugreek and mustard powder mixture and mix well.
Remove from the heat and allow the pickle to cool before transferring to a container. Store it in the refrigerator for longer shelf life.
Ensure the pickle mixture and storage container are fully dry and free from any moisture. Water contact will cause spoilage and reduce shelf life.

recipes.name: Jasmine Rice
steps: Wash the rice 3-4 times and add measured fresh water
Add 2 tbsp oil and set the rice cooker to cook 1.5 hours before you need to serve it
takes approx 1 hour to cook the rice, so time according to when it needs to be served
Wash the rice 3-4 times and add measured fresh water
Start cooking the rice approx 1.5 hours before you need to serve it. Add 2 tbsp oil while cooking
let the rice cook uncovered on medium heat. Once most of the water is absorbed, close the lid and lower the flame
Cook exactly for 15 minutes (set a timer). At the end of 15 minutes switch off the flame. Do not open the lid

recipes.name: Jeera Rice
steps: Wash the basmati rice and drain. Do not let it sit for long as the grain will break when you saute it.
Heat oil in a pot. Add jeera and bay leaf and saute. Add the washed basmati rice to it and salt. Mix properly and saute for 4-5 minutes
Add 2x water and mix. Bring the mixture to a boil. Lower the heat and let it cook on medium-low heat until the surface water is absorbed
Cover the pot with a lid, reduce heat to low and let it cook for 15 minutes (Set a timer). Switch off the flame and let it sit for another 15 minutes.
Open when ready to serve. Overall this will take about 1.5 hours to cook

recipes.name: Kada Prasad
steps: Melt the ghee in a kadai/wok. Note that ghee and sugar are 1-1, and flour and water are 1-1 in volume but not in weight.
Please follow the weights as listed in the recipe above
Add wheat flour and cook till dark golden and aromatic on low flame. Add water and mix well and keep stirring so lumps arent formed
Remember that since you will cook a large quantity add the water before reaching the final desired color as the residual heat will continue
Add sugar and mix properly. Cook till everything comes together and Prasad starts leaving ghee
to bring additional color. Watch the recipe below..
Serve warm

recipes.name: Kadala Curry
steps: Important prep: Rinse the black chana under cold water 2-3 times and add enough water to soak overnight
Pressure cook the black chana with salt and turmeric. Once you the cooker is on pressure let it cook for 25 minutes on low flame. Or cook on stovetop until fully cooked.
Finely chop onions and tomatoes and leave it aside
Roast the coconut mixture: heat up a bit of coconut oil to a wok on medium flame. Add coriander seeds and red chillies and roast until fragrant. Make sure they dont burn. Set aside
Now to the same wok add coconut and roast it until it turns DARK brown. Please do NOT skip this step as this is important for authentic kadala curry.
Grind the coconut along with coriander seeds and chillies with very little to no water
In a large pot add coconut oil. To that add the chopped onion and saute until light brown. Add salt to hasten the process.
Once onion is cooked add the tomato and saute until it cooks. Then add the cooked chana and the coconut paste. Adjust water and bring it to a boil
Finally add a tempering with coconut oil, mustard seeds, hing and curry leaves and add it to the chana

recipes.name: Labra Torkari

ingredients.prep_notes: palm sized piece, peeled, deseeded, cut into 1-inch cubes
or 1 Chinese eggplant, cut into 2-inch cubes

steps: In a pan, dry-roast 2 teaspoons of panch phoron and 2-3 dried red chilies over low heat until fragrant. Once cool, grind into a fine powder.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and add the remaining panch phoron, plus the remaining dried red chilies, bay leaves and one green chili.

Add the vegetables in batches, starting with the potato and sweet potato. Saute for 3 minutes. Next add the pumpkin, then the cauliflower, then the long beans, allowing each to cook a bit before adding the next. After 3-4 minutes, add the cabbage and eggplant and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently.

Add the salt and turmeric. Cover the pan and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are cooked. Add a cup of hot water and mix in (the consistency should not be too runny). Add sugar and labra masala.
To garnish, add a teaspoon of ghee, the remaining slit green chilies and cilantro. Cover and let the curry rest for a few minutes for the flavors to develop before serving.

recipes.name: Langar Wali Dal

ingredients.prep_notes: or to taste, for chili paste

steps: Wash the dals and soak in water for 4 hours, preferably overnight.
When ready to cook, strain the dals and add them to a large pot with 3 cups fresh water, the turmeric and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until soft, about 1 hour.
Once cooked, mash the dal with the back of a ladle.
Grind the ginger, garlic and green chilies into a coarse paste and set aside.
Heat the ghee in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the bay leaf and cumin seeds, and let sizzle. Then add the asafoetida and chili paste, and saute until fragrant.

Add the onion and saute until it turns light brown. Add the turmeric, red chili powder and ground coriander, and saute for a few seconds before adding the tomato. Continue to saute until the ghee begins to separate.
Pour the hot tempering into the cooked dal and mix well. Boil for 10 minutes, adjusting the consistency and salt as needed.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

recipes.name: Lauki Chana Dal Curry
steps: Wash and soak the chana dal for 2 hours.
Blend the chili paste ingredients.
In a saucepan, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, asafoetida and turmeric, and saute until the cumin seeds darken.
Add the chili paste and the chopped onion, and saute until the onion is translucent.
Add the soaked chana dal, tomatoes, salt, ground cumin, garam masala and ground coriander, and saute until tomatoes are cooked.
Add the chopped bottle gourd and mix well to combine. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the bottle gourd is done, about 10-15 minutes.
Garnish with lemon juice and cilantro.

recipes.name: Lauki Sabzi
steps: Peel and Chop lauki into 1 inch cubes
Finely chop onions and tomatoes. Grate or roughly chop ginger and garlic. Ginger garlic paste is also ok
Heat oil, add jeera and hing
Add onions and cook until translucent. Add ginger and garlic and saute well until raw smell is gone
Add tomatoes, salt and cover. Cook till tomatoes fully cook down.
Add turmeric, rest of the salt red chilly powder and saute till masalas are well incorportated and rawness is gone.
Add lauki, cover and let it cook. Stir in between
Can sprinkle water initially but not a lot as lauki will release its own water
When lauki is cooked add garam masala stir, garnish with cilantro

recipes.name: Long Bean Stir Fry

ingredients.prep_notes: or French green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces

steps: In a saucepan, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, asafoetida, onion, dried coconut slices, and green chilies.
Saute until the onion is tender and the coconut is lightly brown (do not fully brown).
Reduce the heat to medium-low, then add the long beans, turmeric, red chili powder and salt. Stir well.
Cover and let cook for 5 minutes, or until the beans are tender but not overcooked.

recipes.name: M'azing Oatmeal
recipes.notes: Cookbook PDF p.30 (manual entry). Includes base oatmeal only; optional topping variations are not fully enumerated.
steps: Bring water to a rolling boil in a medium saucepan.
Add oats with a dash of salt.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until oats are cooked.
Add more water if oatmeal becomes too thick.
Serve with desired sweet or savory toppings.

recipes.name: M's Bhindi (Okra) Fry
steps: Heat coconut oil over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium.
Add onion and green chilies and saute until onion is translucent.
Add turmeric, amchur, and salt.
Add sliced okra and increase heat to medium-high.
Cook, stirring occasionally to prevent burning, until okra is done (7-10 minutes).

recipes.name: M's Cauliflower
steps: Heat coconut oil over medium-high heat and add mustard seeds.
When seeds pop, add dried red chilies and turmeric and saute for 1 minute.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
Reduce heat to medium, add cauliflower, cover, and steam for 2-3 minutes.
Uncover and continue sauteing, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is done.
Add salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: M's Mom's Potato Curry

ingredients.prep_notes: cloves; chili paste, range listed as 3-4

steps: Make the chili paste by blending green chilies, ginger, and garlic.
Heat coconut oil, add ground fennel and potatoes, and saute until lightly browned.
Add salt and turmeric; cook potatoes until about halfway done, then remove and reserve flavored oil.
In the same pan add cumin seeds, onion, and a little salt; saute until onions are translucent.
Add chili paste and tomato puree; cook until tomatoes are done.
Return potatoes, add water as needed, cover, and simmer on low until fully cooked (about 10 minutes).
Crush kasuri methi between palms, add to curry, and adjust seasoning.

recipes.name: M's Plantain Fry
steps: Heat coconut oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Lower to medium, add onion and green chilies, and saute until onion is translucent.
Add turmeric and salt, then add plantains and increase heat to medium-high.
Stir to combine, cover, and cook on medium, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Cook until tender, about 10-12 minutes.

recipes.name: Marathi Kadhi

ingredients.prep_notes: whisked and brought to room temperature

steps: Crush the green chilies and ginger to make a paste.

In a bowl, whisk together the gram flour, chili paste, turmeric, yogurt and salt. Gradually add 2 cups of water, beating until the mixture is smooth and free of lumps. Use room temperature yogurt for best results.

Place the yogurt/water mixture in a pot and bring it to a slow boil over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally so the mixture does not separate. This will take 7-10 minutes to ensure that the gram flour cooks properly and the kadhi thickens. The kadhi should lightly coat the back of a spoon.

Melt the ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add the fenugreek, cumin seeds, asafoetida and curry leaves and saute briefly until aromatic. Add the tempering to the kadhi along with the sugar and stir well.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

recipes.name: Masala & Mint Chai
steps: In a saucepan, bring the water, ginger, and black tea to a boil. Add the milk and bring to a boil again.
Add cardamom powder and mint leaves and bring to a full boil once.
Strain and serve hot.
Pro tip: Do not boil for too long after adding the mint leaves. Avoid adding the stems, as they can make the chai oily.

recipes.name: Masala Chai

ingredients.prep_notes: 2-inch piece, peeled and grated or pounded

steps: Begin with a calm mind.
Boil the water in a pot, add the ginger, and stir. Stir in powdered cardamom.
Add the tea leaves and cook until the water turns dark brown. Simmer over medium-low heat for about 1 minute.
Add the milk and boil until it rises to the top of the pot, then lower the heat so it settles back down. Aerate the tea by stirring it with a ladle or spoon.
Repeat this boiling, cooling, stirring process 2-3 times and switch off the heat.
Add sugar, if desired, and strain into serving cups.

recipes.name: Masala Khichadi
steps: Rinse the rice and dal 2-3 times until the water runs clear. Set aside for about 30 minutes
Thinly slice the onions (okay to cut in 1/4th before or after slicing). Cut the green peppers in 1 inch squares, cauliflower in bite sized florets
Thaw the green peas to room temperature.
In a large pot heat the oil. Add bay leaf followed by mustard seeds. Once they crackle add jeera, hing, turmeric powder, curry leaves.
Saute the onions until translucent, add the green peppers and cauliflower and saute for 1-2 minutes. Add the peas and saute for a few minutes
Add the washed rice and dal and salt. Saute the mixture for 5-6 minutes on medium flame
Add water and turn the flame high and let the water come to a boil. Then lower heat to medium
Add the coriander and jeera powders, garam masala, and mix
Once the water from the surface evaporates, lower the flame and cover and cook it for 15 minutes. once fully cooked garnish with cilantro and serve with ghee

recipes.name: Masala, Mint & Lemongrass Chai
steps: In a saucepan, boil the water with the crushed ginger, chai masala and mint leaves. Cook for 8-10 minutes.
Add the tea leaves and continue to boil for another 3-4 minutes.
Add the milk, and just before the mixture comes to boil, add the lemongrass and cardamom powder. Boil together for 4-5 minutes.
Strain and serve.

recipes.name: Masoor Dal
steps: Wash the dal thoroughly with plenty of water. Soak the dal for 1 hour
Pressure cook the dal until soft and mash it until smooth. Add water to get desired consistency
Heat oil in a pan add black jeera, red chillies, green chilles, bay leaf, turmeric and add it to the whisked dal. Add salt.
Let the dal boil for 4-5 mins. Adjust dal consistency by adding more water.
Garnish with chopped cilantro
https://youtu.be/plb-4p9V6U4?si=j_b_myTlJJlObYfi
https://www.bongeats.com/recipe/plain-mosur-dal

recipes.name: Masoor Dal Tadka
steps: Wash the dal thoroughly until the water runs clear, then soak for 30-60 minutes.
When ready to cook, strain the dal and add to a pot with fresh water to cover. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the dal is soft, about 45-60 minutes.
Mash until smooth and add water to reach the desired consistency (on the thinner side).
To make the tempering, heat the mustard oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the nigella seeds, dried red chilies, bay leaf, turmeric, and green chilies.
Lower the heat and add the dal to the tempering.
Add the salt and allow the dal to boil for 4-5 minutes. Adjust consistency by adding more water if necessary.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

recipes.name: Matar Paneer

ingredients.prep_notes: 3-inch cube, or 1 packet extra-firm tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes

steps: In a frying pan, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil and shallow fry the paneer, turning the pieces to brown on sides. Remove and soak in warm water until ready to add to the gravy.
If using tofu, shallow fry until golden brown on all sides, and place on a paper towel to absorb any excess oil.
Boil water in a small pot, add the peas and a pinch of salt, and cook until done (about 5-7 minutes).

Heat a saucepan over medium heat and add half a tablespoon of oil. Add the onion, garlic and ginger, and saute until the onion turns translucent. Add the tomatoes and cashews and fry until tomatoes are cooked.
Allow the mixture to cool completely and then blend into a smooth paste.

In the same saucepan, heat the remaining half tablespoon of oil over low heat. Add the cumin seeds, turmeric, red chili powder, ground cumin, garam masala and ground coriander, and mix well in the oil until aromatic.
Add the tomato and onion paste, and salt, and cook until the oil separates from the gravy.
Add the cooked peas and the paneer (or tofu), and add hot water for a saucy consistency. Let the curry simmer for 2-3 minutes more.
Garnish with cilantro and crushed kasuri methi.

recipes.name: Mexican Rice
steps: Rinse the rice 2-3 times until the water runs clear. Set aside.
In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, add the oil. Once hot, add the rice and stir to combine
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the rice is lightly roasted all over (about 10 minutes).
Add tomato paste, garlic, and diced onion to the pan and saute for 3-4 minutes. Add bouillion, salt, jalapeno and Tone's cilantro lime mix
Add water (1.25x of the rice). Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low and cook for about 20 minutes or until the water is completely absorbed.
Remove from heat and allow to rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

recipes.name: Mix Vegetable Sambar
steps: Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times in water and soak it with 3x water and some hing and a few drops of oil for 2-4 hours
Pressure cook it: once the pot is at full pressure reduce the heat and let it cookfor 15 minutes
Switch off the flame and let the pressure drop naturally
Once the pressure drops, open the lid and whisk the cooked dal together until its smooth
Dice the onions, bell pepper, melon into 2 inch cubes. Chop the tomatoes into bite sized pieces. Slightly peel and chop drumsticks into 2 inch pieces.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for an hour. Squeeze it with your hands and remove the pulp and set aside
Heat oil and add mustard. When it splutters, add urad dhal, methi, jeera, hing. Then add red chillies and curry leaves
Add diced onions and fry until translucent. Add the tomatoes and fry until cooked.
Add the veg with water, tumeric powder and salt. Keep it covered at medium flame
When it is half-cooked, add tamarind and half of sambar powder.
Once the veg are soft, add the dhal, remaining sambar powder and salt.
When it starts boiling, reduce heat and cover for 5 mins
Garnish with some fresh tempering and cilantro

recipes.name: Mixed Green Salad with Three Dressings
recipes.notes: Cookbook PDF p.56 (manual entry). Includes base salad + three dressing options.

ingredients.ingredient_name: Jaggery or brown sugar or maple syrup

steps: Toss base salad ingredients together in a large bowl, keeping sunflower seeds for garnish.
Blend one dressing option until smooth.
Pour dressing over salad and toss until evenly coated.
Garnish with sunflower seeds and serve.
Variation: choose any one of the three dressings (cilantro lime, sesame ginger, or green goddess).

recipes.name: Mixed Vegetable
steps: Cut potatoes and pumpkin in 1.5 inch cubes
Cut sweet potatoes in 1 inch cubes
Cut cauliflower cabbage beans eggplant in 2 inch cubes
Heat oil and add dried red chillies, bay leaves, one green chilli, and panch phoron.
Add potatoes and sweet potatoes. Fry for 3 minutes
Next, add pumpkin. Fry for 3 minutes.
Add cauliflower and fry for 3 minutes
Then, add long beans, and fry for 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and eggplant. Keep stirring and frying
Add salt and turmeric. Cover the pan and keep cooking the vegetables on low heat, stirring occasionally (about 15 minutes or so).
Add sugar, and continue cooking, covered, for another 10 minutes. The salt and sugar will draw water from the vegetables, and allow them to cook in their own juices
Add some water to help vegetables cook in a large pot, if needed.
Finally, garnish with green chillies, chopped coriander leaves, garam masala. Cover and rest for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Mixed Vegetable Korma

ingredients.prep_notes: half packet, thawed, for coconut paste

steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature.
Crush or blend the thawed coconut, green chilies, fennel seeds and cashews to make a fine paste.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the fennel seeds, bay leaf, cumin seeds, cardamom pods and cloves, and saute until aromatic.
Add the onion and fry until translucent, then add the ginger and garlic. Saute well.
Add the tomatoes and saute until well cooked.
Add the turmeric, salt, chili powder, garam masala and cilantro, and saute for 2-3 minutes.
Add the carrots, cauliflower, potato and peas. Cook for 3-5 minutes until the vegetables are done.
Mix in the coconut paste and cook for 2-3 minutes until aromatic. Add water if necessary to get a thick, gravy-like consistency. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with more cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Mung Dal Payasam
steps: Roast moong dal (unwashed) until it is aromatic. Wash the moong dal, add the water and let it cook until it turns soft. Add water if needed as it cooks
In another pot take the jaggery and add a bit of water and stir until jaggery dissolves completely
Add the cooked mung dal to the jaggery mixture, mix well and simmer for 3-5 minutes
Heat some coconut oil and on low flame and saute the cashews until golden brown. Then saute the coconut slices. Finally saute the raisins until they puff up
Add coconut milk to the mung dal and jaggery mixture and adjust consistency as needed with water
Turn off the flame and add cardamom powder and mix. Add roasted coconut, raisins and cashews and serve

recipes.name: Nolen Gurer Payesh (Bengali Kheer)
steps: Rinse the Gobindobhog Rice and drain a couple of times. Let it sit aside for 30-60 minutes
Transfer the milk to a heavy pan or kadai. On medium heat, wait for it to come to a boil.
Stir regularly so that the milk does not catch the bottom or sides of the pan, dont allow the the cream to form on top
Use a small portion of ghee just enough to out a slight coat on the rice , make sure you dont crush the rice while doing it.
Transfer the rice to the milk, again keep Stirring regularly so that the milk & rice does not catch the bottom or sides of the pan,
Keep cooking on low heat until the rice is fully cooked. This will take time, dont rush it.
The consistency will get thick, you should be able to see the rice appearing at the top.
Melt the date jaggery to a liquid in a separate pot on low heat until liquid. Add sugar and salt and mix and set aside.
Soak the raisins in a little water to allow them to swell. Dry roast the cashews just to make the rawness go away
Keep cooking until a grain of rice easily mashes against your finger - it should be soft and mushy. Keep stirring throughout
Before adding the jaggery it is important that rice is fully cooked as it will stop cooking once jaggery is added.
**Also the milk can separate if jaggery is added earlier when its still on the burner**
Turn off the burner, add the jaggery syrup, dry roasted cashew and soaked rasins
Slowly give it a thorough and even mix. Cover the lid till you serve.

recipes.name: Oatmeal with Toppings
steps: Bring a water to a rolling boil. Important step to ensure that the oatmeal doesnt have a gooey texture
Add Oats and let the oats cook on medium heat
Add a dash of salt and turn to a simmer until cooked through. Add more water if the oatmeal is too thick
Serve with toppings on the side that people can help themselves with
Sweet toppings include bananas, almonds, pecans, maple syrup
savory toppings include chutney podi and ghee

recipes.name: Palak Kadhi
steps: Whisk the yogurt and besan together in a thick paste
Wash and finely chop the spinach. Finely chop the cilantro.
In a large pot melt ghee. Once hot add jeera, hing, turmeric, crushed green chilliles, curry leaves and a little bit of chopped cilantro, and red chilly powder
Add the chopped spinach, salt and give it a good mix and let the spinach cook for 2-3 minutes. Do not cover the pot. Once cooked mash the spinach with a masher or a spoon
Once spinach is cooked add the yogurt+besan mixture and water and mix well
The consistency should be like a thin dal at this stage
Let the kadhi come to a boil on medium heat. Keep stirring so it doesnt separate
It will start to thicken once the besan is cooked. Add remaining cilantro
Optional: Prepare a second seasoning with ghee, jeera, hing and red chilly powder, and add on top of the kadhi just before serving

recipes.name: Panchratna Dal
steps: Wash and soak the dal for 2 hours. Boil on stovetop with 3x water and half the turmeric. Keep stirring occassionally. Remove from heat once fully cooked.
Finely chop the onions and tomatoes and keep aside. Chop the cilantro. Make green chilly-ginger paste.
Heat the oil, add whole red chilli, green chilli jeera, bay leaf, hing. Add ginger and then add chopped onion.
Fry onion until translucent. Add dry spices and mix. Add chopped tomatoes and saute until the tomatoes are cooked and the mixture starts to release oil
Add the cooked dal to it and mix properly. Let it simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes stirring occassionally
Switch off the flame, add lemon juice and garam masala and mix properly. Garnish with cilantro before serving

recipes.name: Plain Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Wash the rice and dal and set aside for about an hour.
In a large pot combine the rice, dal and water. Bring to a boil.
Add the turmeric and black peppercorns, and simmer over medium heat. Add salt once the khichdi is almost done, and mix well.
Keep stirring and add water if needed (consistency should be like thick porridge, but not dry).
Add ghee on top and mix just before serving.
Serve with yogurt or raita, pickle, and salad.

recipes.name: Plain Rice

ingredients.prep_notes: or other varieties such as ambe mor and basmati

steps: Wash the rice 3-4 times and soak in 2 cups water for 15-30 minutes.
Transfer the rice and soaking water to a pot and cook over medium heat, uncovered, until it comes to a boil.
Once most of the water has been absorbed, cover, and lower the heat. Cook exactly for 15 minutes (a timer may be helpful) and switch off the heat.
Let the rice sit for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Optionally, add a teaspoon of ghee to the rice once it starts to boil.

recipes.name: Poha (Flattened Rice)
steps: Wash and drain poha, rest about 20 minutes, then gently fluff.
Heat oil over medium heat and add mustard, cumin, fennel, asafoetida, chilies, and curry leaves.
Add onion and turmeric; saute until onion is translucent.
Add potato and salt and cook over medium-low until potato is done.
Add soaked poha and gently mix to coat with tempering.
Cover and cook on low for a couple minutes, then sprinkle about 1/4 cup water and steam 2-3 more minutes.
Turn off heat, add lemon/lime juice and cilantro, adjust salt, and mix gently.

recipes.name: Potato Sabzi
steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature.
Boil the potatoes in their skins until cooked through. Allow them to cool, then remove their skins and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Make a paste of green chilies and ginger. Finely chopping them will also do.
Heat the oil over medium heat in a large frying pan or wok. Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add the cumin seeds, asafoetida and turmeric, and saute until the cumin seeds darken.
Add the chili paste, curry leaves, one quarter of the chopped cilantro, and salt. Saute for about a minute.
Add the potatoes and mix thoroughly. Add the sugar and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 7-10 minutes until the potatoes are lightly browned.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice, and garnish with the remaining cilantro and a bit more finely grated coconut.

recipes.name: Purple Cabbage Salad
steps: Shred the cabbage into thin long pieces. Thaw the coconut to room temperature. Finely chop the cilantro
Mix together cabbage, coconut, cilantro, lemon juice, salt and pepper
Cut green chilies about 1 inch in size
Heat up coconut oil in a pan. Once hot add mustard seeds, jeera, hing, ginger, chillies and curry leaves and add the tempering to the salad
Mix it all up. Garnish with some cilantro before serving
Adjust salt and lemon juice based on taste

recipes.name: Quinoa Salad
steps: Rinse quinoa, add 1 cup water, bring to boil, then simmer uncovered until water is absorbed (10-12 minutes).
Rest quinoa 5 minutes to fluff.
Combine chickpeas, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and cilantro in a large bowl.
Blend dressing ingredients together.
When quinoa is warm (not hot), add to vegetables.
Pour dressing over salad and toss to combine.
Rest 10-15 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Radish Salad

ingredients.prep_notes: medium white or red, thinly sliced or grated

steps: Toss radishes with salt, lemon/lime juice, and cilantro.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Rajma
steps: Soak: Rajma overnight. Prep: Chop onions. Coarsely grind tomatoes. Grind ginger garlic green chilli into a paste. Julienne ginger and chop cilantro for garnish
Boil : Add the required amount of water and salt and boil the rajama until cooked properly. If using a pressure cooker let it cook on slow flame
for 15 minutes after the cooker is at full pressure
Tempering : In a pan add oil. When hot add jeera and saute until they crackle. Add coarsely ground green chilli, ginger and garlic paste and saute for a min
Saute onion with Tumeric powder, corander powder, and salt until the onions turn light brown
Saute for a few mins then add tomatoes and saute it until the mixture starts to leave oil on the sides
Drain the liquid from the cooked rajma and reserve on the side. Add rajma (without the cooking water) and fry the beans with the masala
Then add the reserved water. Let it simmer on low flame for 10-15 minutes. Add garam masala at the end and remove from flame.
Garnish it with Cilantro and ginger julienne

recipes.name: Raw Mango Pickle
steps: Place the mango pieces in a bowl. Add the red chili powder, salt, mustard seed powder, roasted fenugreek powder, turmeric, garlic and asafoetida.
Pour in the oil and combine thoroughly until the mango pieces are well coated.
Keep covered for 12-24 hours in a cool, dry spot to let the flavors develop.
Adjust the salt and chili powder to taste, and enjoy.
Store in a clean, dry glass container in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Red Cabbage Salad

ingredients.prep_notes: includes pinch for chili paste, then to taste

steps: Thaw coconut to room temperature.
Crush chopped green chili with a pinch of salt into a paste.
Mix cabbage, onion, coconut, cilantro, lemon/lime juice, ginger, peanuts, and green chili paste.
Heat oil/ghee and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and urad dal until dal turns golden.
Add asafoetida and curry leaves, then pour tempering into the salad.
Mix thoroughly and adjust salt and lemon juice.
Garnish with cilantro before serving.

recipes.name: Red Pumpkin Curry
steps: In a saucepan, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the bay leaves, fenugreek, cumin seeds, asafoetida, dried red chilies and green chilies. Saute for a minute, then add the tomatoes and cook until the oil is released.
Add the turmeric, red chili powder, ground coriander, garam masala and ginger, plus a little water to prevent the spices from burning.
Add the pumpkin and salt, and mix well to combine. Cover the pan and cook for 8-10 minutes until the pumpkin is cooked through.
Add the dried raw mango powder at the very end, which will add a distinctive sour taste.
Garnish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Rice (Ambe Mor)
steps: Plan this 2.5 hours before meal time
Soak rice in a pot for an hour with the measured quantity of water (usually 2x)
Add salt and oil to the soaked rice and start cooking the rice approx 1.5 hours before you need to serve it
let the rice cook uncovered. Once most of the water is absorbed, close the lid and lower the flame
Cook exactly for 15 minutes (set a timer). At the end of 15 minutes switch off the flame. Do not open the lid
Let it sit for 30 min before you open and turn the rice for serving

recipes.name: Rice (Basmati)
steps: Wash the rice 3-4 times and soak it in measured fresh water for 1 hour in the rice cooker
Set the rice cooker to cook 1.5 hours before you need to serve the rice
takes approx 1 hour to cook the rice, so time according to when it needs to be served

recipes.name: Rice (Kerala Matta)
steps: Wash the rice 3-4 times and soak it in measured fresh water for 3.5 hours in the rice cooker
Add 2 tbsp oil and set the rice cooker to cook 1.5 hours before you need to serve it
takes approx 1 hour to cook the rice, so time according to when it needs to be served

recipes.name: Rice (Sona Masoori)
steps: Wash the rice 3-4 times and soak it in measured fresh water for 1 hour in the rice cooker
Set the rice cooker to cook 1.5 hours before you need to serve the rice
takes approx 1 hour to cook the rice, so time according to when it needs to be served

recipes.name: Rice Kheer
steps: Rinse the rice a few times in water and drain. Let sit for 15-20 minutes.
Crush the saffron lightly between your fingers and soak in 1 tablespoon of warm milk.
Melt the ghee over medium-low in a small pan and saute the cashews and raisins until cashews are golden brown and raisins puff up.
Bring the water to a boil in a small pot. Add the soaked rice and cook over medium-low until done, about 5-7 minutes (keep watch as the water can boil off quickly).

Stir in the milk and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 20-30 minutes until the milk reduces, stirring periodically to avoid scorching. Mash the rice slightly until the kheer turns creamy. Add more milk as needed to achieve the correct consistency.

Add the sugar and stir well. Continue to cook for another 3-5 minutes until the sugar dissolves completely. Add the roasted nuts and raisins and turn off the heat. Add the cardamom and saffron/milk mixture, and mix thoroughly.
The kheer will thicken slightly as it cools down. It is typically served slightly warm, but also tastes delicious when cold.

recipes.name: Roasted Corn Salad
steps: Slice red onions, finely chop the jalapenos, dice the tomatoes. Thaw the charred corn to room temperature
In a bowl, mix together the onions, jalapeños, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper. Keep aside for 20 minutes to 1 hour to let it marinate
Add the charred corn to the marinated onions. Add in the diced tomatoes
Season to taste with salt and pepper and a squeeze of extra lemon juice
Wash and shred the romaine lettuce and serve on the side

recipes.name: Saffron and Rose Chai
steps: Pour the water into a pan. Crush the saffron strands between your fingers and add to the water, along with the tea leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 3-4 minutes. The fragrance of the saffron will be prominent, indicating that its ready for the next step.
Add the crushed cardamom, rose petals, and nutmeg, along with the milk.

Increase the heat and bring to a boil. As the chai rises to the surface, lower the heat so it does not boil over. Increase the heat again and let the mixture rise almost to the surface, and then lower the heat again. Repeat this cycle another 4-5 times.
Stir in the sugar, if desired, and serve hot.

recipes.name: Sambar (Drumstick, Plantain & Arbi)

ingredients.prep_notes: fresh, or half packet frozen, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
medium, outer skin peeled, cut into 1-inch cubes
arbi, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces

steps: Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times and soak in water with a pinch of asafoetida and a few drops of oil for at least 1-2 hours.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for an hour. Make into a paste and set aside.

In a medium-sized pot, boil the drumsticks, plantain, tomato and taro roots in water with the turmeric. Cover and simmer over medium heat. When halfway done, around 8-10 minutes, add the tamarind paste and half of the sambar powder.
Once the vegetables are soft, add the cooked dal, remaining sambar powder and salt.
Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 3-4 minutes. You may leave the pot partially covered, but stir occasionally to ensure the sambar does not boil over.

To make the tempering, heat the oil in a pan. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek, asafoetida, dried red chilies and curry leaves. Pour the tempering into the sambar and garnish with cilantro to serve.

recipes.name: Sambar (Green Pepper)

ingredients.prep_notes: lime-sized ball, or 3 tbsp tamarind paste
medium, finely chopped, optional, for tempering

steps: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 1-2 hours, if not using paste. After soaking, squeeze it with your hands, remove the fibers and set the tamarind pulp aside.
Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times, then soak it with a pinch of asafoetida in 3 cups of fresh water for 30-60 minutes.
Put 2 cups of water in a saucepan and add the tomatoes, green pepper and onion. Bring to a boil.
Add the sambar powder, salt and tamarind pulp, and continue to boil until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the cooked dal and mix thoroughly. Adjust the consistency by adding more water (it should be thin).

In a small pan, heat the oil and add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek, asafoetida, turmeric, dried red chilies and curry leaves. (Optionally, add some finely chopped onion and saute until light brown.)
Add the tempering to the sambar, give it a good stir, and garnish with cilantro just before serving.

recipes.name: Sambar (Red Onion)

ingredients.prep_notes: whole, or 1 medium red onion diced

steps: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 1 hour. Squeeze it with your hands and remove the fiber, and then set aside, reserving the soaking water.
Thoroughly rinse the toor dal in water until the water is clear. Soak it in 3 cups of water and a pinch of asafoetida for 30-60 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek, asafoetida, turmeric, dried red chilies and curry leaves, and saute for 5-7 seconds.
Add the onions and saute until translucent. Add the tomato and salt, and saute until the tomato is well cooked.
Add the sambar powder and saute for 1-2 minutes, then pour in the tamarind water and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the cooked dal and stir to combine. Adjust the salt and sambar powder if needed.
Garnish with cilantro before serving.

recipes.name: Sambar (Varutharacha)

ingredients.prep_notes: medium, finely diced, for coconut paste

steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature. Soak the tamarind in water for 1 hour.

Rinse the toor dal and soak it in water and a pinch of asafoetida for 1 hour. Place the soaked dal in a pot with water to cover and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until cooked, about 1 hour.
To make the coconut paste, roast all ingredients in a pan over medium heat, and then grind to a paste.
Make tamarind paste by squeezing the soaked tamarind with your hands and removing the fibers.

Add 1 1/2 cups of water to a saucepan along with the drumsticks, eggplants, tomato and onion. Bring to a boil and cook for 1-2 minutes. Add the tamarind paste and cooked dal. Once the raw smell of the tamarind is gone, add the coconut paste and salt, and simmer for a few minutes.

Make the tempering by heating the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, fenugreek, dried red chilies, asafoetida and curry leaves and saute for 5-7 seconds. Pour the tempering into the sambar and adjust for salt.
Remove from the heat, cover and let the flavours mingle before garnishing with cilantro and serving.

recipes.name: Sambar Powder
steps: Dry roast the jeera and methi separately (without oil)
Roast all the other ingredients separately with a little bit of oil
Let it cool. Grind to a fine powder
Once its completely cooled store in airtight containers. Divide it into 4-5 identical containers

recipes.name: Simple Dal Tadka
steps: Wash Toor dal and soak for 1-2 hours
Pressure Cook dal with turmeric and a little salt (1:3 water ratio) and then whisk it to mix it well
Take about 20% of the dal aside for vegan serving
For the regular dal: bring the dal to a boil. Separately make a seasoning with ghee, jeera, hing, red chillies. Add to the dal and mix
Add lemon juice and chopped cilantro and switch off the flame
For vegan dal follow the same process but make the seasoning with oil instead of ghee

recipes.name: Sliced Carrots and Cucumber
steps: Slice Carrots and cucumbers in the food processor
Add salt, black pepper, and mix well
Add lemon juice concentrate
Garnish with cilantro

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong with Khakra
steps: Important Prep: Wash and soak the moong for about 8 hours. Drain the water, cover it with a piece of cloth to let them sprout
Take a large pot and transfer the sprouted moong and water. Add salt and turmeric and let it cook partially covered until soft
Once the moong has cooked, remove about 20% of it aside to make a tadka with coconut oil. Rest will have seasoning with ghee
Vegan: In a pan heat up coconut oil. When hot add mustard seeds, jeera, hing, little turmeric, coriander powder, some cilantro
Switch off the flame, add red chilly powder and mix. Add the seasoning to the vegan portion of the cooked moong
For the regular seasoning make it the same style as vegan, except use ghee instead of coconut oil
Add lemon juice and cilantro and mix well. Adjust for salt and the moong are ready to serve
Serve with khakra on the side - this type of breakfast is consumed in rajasthan / kutch region of india
The consistency should be llike oatmeal and the moong should be almost mushy with some retaining their shape

recipes.name: Sprouted Savory Moong with Khakhra
steps: Wash and soak moong for about 8 hours.
Drain, cover with cloth, and sprout for about 16-24 hours.
Cook sprouted moong with about twice the water, plus salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric, until soft.
Heat ghee and add mustard, cumin, asafoetida, remaining turmeric, ground coriander, and half the cilantro.
Turn off heat, add red chili powder, and mix.
Stir seasoning into cooked moong.
Add lemon/lime juice and remaining cilantro, then adjust salt.
Serve with khakhra.

recipes.name: Thai Curry with Vegetables & Tofu

ingredients.prep_notes: medium head, cut into bite sized florets
medium, cut into bite sized florets
1 pack, or fried tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
as needed; curry pastes are typically salted

steps: Put a kettle on to boil.
Scoop out 2 tablespoons of thick coconut cream from the top of the canned coconut milk and add it to a pot over medium heat. Cook until it begins to release oil.
Add the curry paste and saute until fragrant. Add the broccoli and cauliflower, and stir.
Once the vegetables are somewhat tender, add the bamboo shoots and tofu and continue to saute.
After 5-7 minutes, but before the vegetables are fully done, add the red bell pepper and the remaining coconut milk. Simmer for a few minutes, taking care that the red pepper remains crunchy.
Add one half cup of the boiling water and mix well. Avoid overcooking.
Taste for salt and spice level. Add more curry paste if desired, and stir in the cilantro.
All vegetables should be cooked with a slight crunch and not be mushy.

recipes.name: Tomato Cucumber Romaine Salad
steps: Wash and dry cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce and cilantro. Peel the cucumbers if they are waxy.
Cut cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce into 1 inch bite sized cubes
Add salt, pepper, olive oil, lemon juice and mix well
Garnish with cilantro and serve

recipes.name: Tomato Salsa
steps: Chop the onions, garlic and jalapenos in a food processor. Lightly pulse the tomatoes in the food processor separately.
Finely chop the cilantro. Mix everything together in a bowl. Add salt, pepper, lemon juice and mix
Refrigerate it for a few hours before serving

recipes.name: Undhiyu
steps: Prep the vegetables: Quarter the eggplant vertically. Peel the outer green skin of plantain with a peeler, cut it vertically in half and 4 horizontal parts. Store covered in water.
Peel the sweet potato, cut it vertically in half and 3-4 horizontal parts so each part is about 1.5 inches long and wide. Store covered in water
Peel the potato and split them in 4 pieces, store in covered water. Thaw all the frozen vegetables.
Lightly pulse the coconut to make it into a rough powder. Make a coarse powder of sesame seeds.
In a bowl mix together the coconut, sesame seed powder, jeera and coriander powder, red chili powder, and salt.
Take a pot, add the oil. Lightly crush the ajwain in between your palms and add to the oil. Add some salt to taste
Layer all the vegetables with the eggplants and plantains on the top. Add plenty of water so it can cook without the vegetables getting stuck to the bottom of the pan
Cover the lid of the pot, and start the flame on medium and let the vegetables cook for 20-35 minutes
Add the coconut-sesame-spice mixture and mix well. Cover and continue to cook until the vegetables are cooked properly
